title: enable builds with address sanitizer and possibly other instrumentations
build libcuml 22.x
description:
- Check https://github.com/rapidsai/cuml/releases for stable releases of libcuml
- Try adding 22.x to https://github.com/mlverse/libcuml-builds/blob/e7c5b494a2d9a7918f393d9a34cadf6ce1a5ae63/.github/workflows/cuml.yml#L14 once libcuml 22.x is released. In the best case scenario, the build will succeed after about 2 hours [*]. If not, then you may need to make some (hopefully minor) 22.x-specific adjustments to the build process to make it work.
- Finally, make a PR in the {cuda.ml} repo to add the new libcuml version to https://github.com/mlverse/cuda.ml/blob/d76add4d93950b1c85356823afe00bd11867ff8d/.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml#L18, and hope all existing features work with this new version of libcuml.

[*] As you may have noticed, the builds are now incremental. So, once you add a new version, only the new version of libcuml will be built because the GitHub action workflow sees there are already pre-built versions of libcuml 21.x that are released. Therefore to re-build and re-release an existing supported libcuml version (should it become necessary), you must delete the existing release and re-run this workflow manually. The "re-build and re-release" scenario seems highly unlikely though. I highly doubt we'll ever run into it.
